To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
ethanolic extracts obtained from 14 plants showed a certain antibacterial activity, whereas 5 extracts displayed a significant cytotoxic activity.
14 of the ethanolics extracts of Yemeni medicinal plant species showed a moderate antibacterial activity, whereas five extracts were found to be cytotoxic.
the most active ethanolic extract was obtained from Lawsonia inermus, followed by Aloe perry, Indigoferia oblongifolia and Meriandra benguhalensis.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of new antibacterial and cytostatic compounds from medicinal plants used in Yemen.
the screening of 20 Yemeni medicinal plants used by traditional healers in the treatment of infectious diseases for their antibacterial and cytotoxical activity.
the identification of new antibacterial agents from Yemeni medicinal plants, and it may contribute to the development of new drugs to combat infectious diseases in developing countries.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the ethanolic extract of L. inermis is the most active antibacterial extract, while extracts of C. procera, C. murale, P. orientalis, T. terrestris and W. somniferum are the most cytotoxic ones.
some of the ethanomic extracts of Yemeni medicinal plant species showed antibacterial and cytotoxical activities and thus could be used in further investigations.
the investigated ethanolic extracts are promising candidates for the isolation and purification of new antibacterial compounds.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
some of the plants used in traditional medicine by Yemeni people have a significant potential for the development of new drugs.
the traditional use of these medicinal plants is supported by our results, and that the ethanolic extract of Lawsonia Inermis is a promising source of antibacterial substances.
some of the plants investigated are promising sources of new antibacterial and cytotoxical substances, which could be of interest for further research.
The main takeaway from our work is that
many of the plants used in traditional medicinal practice in Yemen are indeed effective against the tested bacteria and/or against the FL-cells.
some of the tested plant species may be a good source for the development of new antibacterial drugs.
the traditional knowledge of medicinal plant usage by the Yemeni people can be a valuable source for the identification of plants with antibacterial activity.
